speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if you recall any specific event, like a bite or injury, that started it? Additionally, have you noticed any fever or swelling around the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the rapid progression of the ulcer following the reported ant bite (which may have been coincidental or a minor trauma triggering the condition), I suspect this is an inflammatory ulcer rather than an infectious one. Can you tell me if the pain is disproportionately severe compared to the size of the wound, and have you noticed any bluish or purple borders around the lesion?
